dossier.purpose: Python library (PyPI `openai-agents` 0.23.0, MIT; pyproject.toml:2-7) providing an Agent/Runner loop with function, hosted, MCP-client and agent-as-tool tools, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, tracing, Realtime/Voice, and a `SandboxAgent` runtime (manifest-defined workspaces; shell/filesystem/skills/memory/compaction capabilities; Unix-local, Docker and seven hosted sandbox clients; snapshots; resumable `RunState` and sandbox session state). The docs call the sandbox runtime an 'execution harness' (docs/sandbox_agents.md:5). It is a library only: no CLI, daemon, server or MCP server is shipped (pyproject.toml has no [project.scripts]). Default model provider is OpenAI (Responses API); other providers go through OpenAI-compatible endpoints or best-effort beta LiteLLM/Any-LLM adapters (docs/models/index.md:683-705). There is no packaged deep-research harness: research exists only as examples (examples/research_bot, examples/financial_research_agent) built on the OpenAI-hosted WebSearchTool. Model names in code, docs and examples top out at `gpt-5.6-sol` (src/agents/models/default_models.py:66); the string 'GPT-6.1 Sol' (or any `gpt-6*` identifier) appears nowhere in the repository (repo-wide search, generated translations excluded).

claims.claim: "The OpenAI Agents SDK is a lightweight yet powerful framework for building multi-agent workflows. It is provider-agnostic, supporting the OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs, as well as 100+ other LLMs."
Sandbox agents: "Agents preconfigured to work with a container to perform work over long time horizons."
Tools: "Various Tools let agents take actions (functions, MCP, hosted tools)"
Human in the loop: "Built-in mechanisms for involving humans across agent runs"
Sessions: "Automatic conversation history management across agent runs"
Tracing: "Built-in tracking of agent runs, allowing you to view, debug and optimize your workflows"
"Set the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable before running any of these examples."
"Use a SandboxAgent when the agent needs to inspect files, run commands, apply patches, or preserve workspace state across longer tasks."
"This example uses UnixLocalSandboxClient, which is supported on macOS and Linux. On Windows, use DockerSandboxClient with the openai-agents[docker] extra or a hosted sandbox client instead"
The sandbox example clones `GitRepo(repo="openai/openai-agents-python", ref="main")` into the manifest and runs with `UnixLocalSandboxClient()`
"Pull requests are limited to repository collaborators; we do not accept pull requests from non-collaborators." Security issues: follow SECURITY.md
Optional dependencies include websockets, SQLAlchemy, any-llm and LiteLLM

install.command: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install openai-agents

install.method: pip extra for the Docker sandbox client
pip extras for hosted sandbox clients (blaxel, cloudflare, daytona, e2b, modal, runloop, vercel) and model adapters (litellm, any-llm)

install.command: make sync   # runs: uv sync --all-extras --all-packages --group dev

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - pure-Python package (hatchling wheel of src/agents only, pyproject.toml:140-154), requires-python >=3.10 (pyproject.toml:6); CI test matrix runs on ubuntu-latest for Python 3.10-3.14 (.github/workflows/tests.yml:119-161); runner CPU arch is not stated in the workflow. UnixLocalSandboxClient is supported on Linux (README.md:77) but adds no OS-level confinement there (src/agents/sandbox/sandboxes/unix_local.py:752-753).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - no WSL2 mention in README or docs and no WSL2 CI job (only reference is a comment about Git for Windows Bash vs the WSL launcher, tests/test_change_detection.py:72). Code branches on sys.platform, so a WSL2 distro would presumably take the Linux paths (inference only, not tested).
platforms.macos_arm64: yes - README.md:77 says Unix-local sandboxing is supported on macOS; CI job `native-macos-sandbox` runs `uv run pytest -m requires_native_macos_sandbox` on macos-latest (.github/workflows/tests.yml:191-219; runner arch not stated). macOS commands are wrapped in `sandbox-exec` (filesystem restrictions only, no network isolation) and fail with ExecTransportError if `sandbox-exec` is not on PATH (src/agents/sandbox/sandboxes/unix_local.py:745-774).
platforms.gpu: no - client library with no local GPU use. Only the Modal hosted sandbox client exposes a `gpu` option (src/agents/extensions/sandbox/modal/sandbox.py:295); the Docker client options are image, exposed_ports, network_mode ('none' only) and labels (src/agents/sandbox/sandboxes/docker.py:220-250).

integrations.cli: none found - pyproject.toml has no [project.scripts]; the only terminal helper is the Python function `run_demo_loop` (src/agents/repl.py:15); the only `__main__` blocks are internal helper workers (src/agents/sandbox/sandboxes/_docker_removal_worker.py:337, src/agents/sandbox/sandboxes/_unix_local_file_ops.py:318).
integrations.mcp: client side only: MCPServerStdio/MCPServerSse/MCPServerStreamableHttp (src/agents/mcp/server.py:1962,2112,2290), MCPServerManager (src/agents/mcp/manager.py:260) and the OpenAI-hosted `HostedMCPTool` (src/agents/tool.py:1136; docs/mcp.md:20-25). No MCP server exposing the SDK was found (src imports only mcp client modules, src/agents/mcp/server.py:20-24).
integrations.sdk_or_api: Python SDK: `agents.Runner` (src/agents/run.py:259), `agents.sandbox.SandboxAgent` (src/agents/sandbox/sandbox_agent.py:31). The JS/TS SDK is a separate repository (README.md:8). No HTTP API server is shipped: FastAPI is a dev-only dependency (pyproject.toml:121) and the only `FastAPI(` string in src is a docstring example (src/agents/mcp/manager.py:283).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Codex: experimental `codex_tool` runs the separately installed `codex` CLI as a subprocess (`codex exec --experimental-json`) with sandbox_mode read-only/workspace-write/danger-full-access and approval policies (src/agents/extensions/experimental/codex/exec.py:61-132; thread_options.py:9-12; docs/tools.md:890-952). The repo also carries maintainer-facing Codex skills under .agents/skills/*/agents/openai.yaml (AGENTS.md:27-34; .agents/skills/code-change-verification/agents/openai.yaml:1-4) - not a user integration. Claude Code: none found (no CLAUDE.md, .claude/, plugin or MCP server).

readme.telemetry_and_network: Tracing is ON by default and exports to OpenAI: BatchTraceProcessor + BackendSpanExporter post traces/spans to https://api.openai.com/v1/traces/ingest with the OPENAI_API_KEY bearer token (src/agents/tracing/processors.py:46,175-179,903-922; src/agents/tracing/setup.py:52-60; docs/tracing.md:5-13,29-45). `trace_include_sensitive_data` (LLM and tool inputs/outputs) defaults to true (src/agents/run_config.py:53-56,414-420). Disable with OPENAI_AGENTS_DISABLE_TRACING=1, set_tracing_disabled(True) or RunConfig.tracing_disabled (src/agents/tracing/provider.py:339-356; docs/tracing.md:7-11); tracing is unavailable for ZDR orgs (docs/tracing.md:13); with no key the exporter logs a warning and skips export (processors.py:146); custom processors can add or replace destinations (docs/tracing.md:59); non-OpenAI setups get 401s unless tracing is disabled or given a key (docs/models/index.md:609-615). A configured harness ID is added to trace metadata only (src/agents/models/openai_agent_registration.py:74-87; docs/config.md:111-127). No analytics/telemetry library found in src (searched); model calls send header `User-Agent: Agents/Python <version>` (src/agents/models/openai_responses.py:113-114); the MongoDB session identifies the library in the driver handshake (src/agents/extensions/memory/mongodb_session.py:72). Model/tool payload logging is off by default (docs/config.md:236-250; src/agents/_debug.py:13-17). Required services/accounts: an OpenAI API key for the default provider (docs/config.md:36; OPENAI_BASE_URL can redirect, docs/config.md:84). Optional: Docker daemon and image pulls for the Docker client (src/agents/sandbox/sandboxes/docker.py:1868-1870); a separate provider account/key for each hosted sandbox (examples/sandbox/extensions/README.md:11,23,88-89,128-134,181-190,222,246,328-329), whose adapters are not live-validated in CI (examples/sandbox/extensions/README.md:165); `GitRepo` manifest entries `git clone` from github.com (default host) inside the sandbox (src/agents/sandbox/entries/artifacts.py:739-769); rclone-based mounts apt-install tools and download a SHA-256-pinned rclone from downloads.rclone.org inside the sandbox (src/agents/extensions/sandbox/_rclone.py:11-26,51-90); the Codex tool needs a separately installed codex CLI plus CODEX_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY (docs/tools.md:939-941).

languages: Markdown docs with generated ja/ko/zh translations (pyproject.toml:161-163)

entry_points.what: `Runner.run` / `run_sync` / `run_streamed` (run.py:259-469) delegating to `AgentRunner` (run.py:548); main programmatic entry point (README.md:58-69).
`UnixLocalSandboxClient` (:1518): host-process sandbox; sandbox-exec filesystem restrictions on macOS only, no confinement on Linux (:745-774).
`DockerSandboxClient` / `DockerSandboxClientOptions` (:220): container backend, optional network_mode='none'; needs the `docker` extra and a Docker daemon.
Hosted sandbox clients blaxel/, cloudflare/, daytona/, e2b/, modal/, runloop/, vercel/ (same-named extras; src/agents/extensions/sandbox/__init__.py:1-80).
MCP client wrappers MCPServerStdio (:1962), MCPServerSse (:2112), MCPServerStreamableHttp (:2290); MCPServerManager in manager.py:260. No MCP server.
`run_demo_loop` terminal REPL helper (:15) - a function, not a console script. No binary, CLI or server main exists in the package.

code.architecture: Single package `src/agents` (the wheel packages only this directory, pyproject.toml:153-154). Core loop: agent.py, run.py (Runner/AgentRunner), run_config.py (RunConfig, ToolExecutionConfig, SandboxRunConfig, DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS=10), run_state.py (resumable JSON RunState, schema 1.18, forward-incompatible by design: lines 205-212), run_internal/ (run loop, tool execution, approvals, session persistence, retries), tool.py (FunctionTool, hosted tools, ShellTool, ApplyPatchTool, CustomTool), guardrail.py and tool_guardrails.py, handoffs/, items.py, result.py. Models: models/ (OpenAIResponsesModel, OpenAIChatCompletionsModel, OpenAIProvider, MultiProvider prefix routing openai/, litellm/, any-llm/; default_models.py with regex-based GPT-5.x settings) and extensions/models/ (LiteLLM and Any-LLM adapters). Persistence: memory/ (Session ABC, SQLiteSession defaulting to ':memory:', OpenAI conversation/compaction sessions) and extensions/memory/ (SQLAlchemy, Redis, MongoDB, Dapr, encrypted, async/advanced SQLite). Tracing: tracing/ (spans, BatchTraceProcessor, default exporter to OpenAI). MCP client: mcp/. Sandbox: sandbox/ (SandboxAgent, Manifest and entries/mounts, capabilities Shell/Filesystem/Skills/Memory/Compaction, session and client abstractions, snapshots incl. LocalSnapshot/RemoteSnapshot/NoopSnapshot, runtime and runtime_session_manager, memory generation), sandbox/sandboxes/ (unix_local, docker, docker_removal opt-in host-side removal service), extensions/sandbox/<provider>/ plus shared _rclone.py. Other: extensions/experimental/codex/ (Codex CLI tool), extensions/experimental/hosted_multi_agent/ (OpenAI beta, WebSocket), realtime/, voice/, testing/ (ScriptedModel etc., tests/README.md:7), repl.py. Research content is example-only and not in the wheel: examples/research_bot (planner -> parallel WebSearchTool search agents -> writer; no citation handling) and examples/financial_research_agent (adds URL-citation and retrieved-source extraction via examples/web_search_utils.py:20-79, writer instructed to cite supplied URLs, an LLM verifier agent comparing against allowed_source_urls, one revision pass then RuntimeError, MAX_SEARCHES=15; manager.py:106-123,256-273; planner_agent.py:5,36).
code.packaging_and_release: Build backend hatchling (pyproject.toml:140-142); wheel contains only src/agents (pyproject.toml:153-154); sdist excludes .agents, .github, .tmp*, .uv*, integration_tests (pyproject.toml:144-151). Artifacts: wheel + sdist from `uv build` (.github/workflows/publish.yml:114-116), kept as a 7-day workflow artifact (publish.yml:117-124), published to PyPI by `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` (SHA-pinned) in a job with environment `pypi` and `id-token: write` (OIDC trusted publishing, no registry token; publish.yml:126-158). No checksum files, signing, SBOM or explicit `attestations:` input appear in the workflows (searched .github and Makefile); .github/RELEASING.md:39,81 says provenance must be verified separately. Release flow: Release Please PR (release-please.yml; release-please-config.json:1-32) -> Release Candidate freezes the public-API contract (release-candidate.yml:55-123) -> maintainer runs a local Codex review and posts a GitHub Approve with a marker line that gates 'Release readiness' (release-readiness.yml:14-32; RELEASING.md:3-44) -> merge -> tag/GitHub Release (when RELEASE_AUTOMATION_ENABLED) -> publish.yml checks tag == release SHA, ancestry in main and tag == pyproject version (.github/scripts/verify_release.py:26-45), re-runs `make sync tests` on Python 3.10-3.14 plus typecheck (publish.yml:66-70), builds on a separate runner and re-verifies approval before upload (publish.yml:143-158). 0.23.0 is dated 2026-10-01 (CHANGELOG.md:3); tag v0.23.0 = commit ce8ae9f (.git/packed-refs:2). Versioning is 0.Y.Z where minor bumps may break non-beta interfaces and patch releases may change beta features (docs/release.md:3-18).
code.tests_and_ci: Frameworks: pytest>=9.0.3 with pytest-asyncio (auto mode), pytest-xdist (`-n auto --maxprocesses=9 --dist worksteal` plus a serial phase), pytest-mock, inline-snapshot; coverage gate `--fail-under=85` (Makefile:84-94,205-210; pyproject.toml:95-102,256-272); mypy --strict, pyright, ruff (pyproject.toml:157-197; Makefile:34-67). Test dirs: tests/ holds about 376 test_*.py files (159 top-level; 63 in tests/sandbox; 103 across tests/{models,mcp,realtime,voice,fastapi}; 26 in tests/extensions; 9 in tests/memory; 11 in tests/tracing; 5 elsewhere; counted from file listings); integration_tests/ holds 31 test_*.py files (packaged wheel/sdist contract, Docker security and containers profiles, live OpenAI/provider/hosted/realtime/voice profiles that need a service-account key; excluded from distributions; integration_tests/README.md:3-17); 6 helper-script tests under .agents/skills and .github/scripts. Provider-neutral fakes (ScriptedModel, scripted_sandbox_session) are the preferred test double (tests/README.md:7); hosted-sandbox adapter tests are fake/mock based (tests/extensions/sandbox/) and the hosted examples are not live-validated in CI (examples/sandbox/extensions/README.md:165). Coverage measurement omits src/agents/sandbox/sandboxes/*.py, mounts, materialization and several sandbox utils (pyproject.toml:227-243), although those modules have dedicated tests (tests/sandbox/test_unix_local*.py, test_docker*.py). A Docker-backed security test checks a model-driven shell cannot read the trusted client credential (integration_tests/security/test_local_sandbox_isolation.py:113-140). CI workflows in .github/workflows: tests.yml (lint; typecheck; mypy --platform win32; tests on ubuntu for Python 3.10-3.14 with coverage on 3.14 and asyncio-stability on 3.10/3.14; Docker `containers`; macOS `native-macos-sandbox`; MCP v1 compat; packaged-contract on 3.10, 3.14 and Windows; prospective-release-contract; tests-windows 3.10/3.13; build-docs), codeql.yml (python + actions; push, PR, merge queue, weekly), docs.yml (build and deploy docs to gh-pages), publish.yml, release-please.yml, release-candidate.yml, release-readiness.yml, repo-skills.yml, issues.yml (stale-issue closer). Test jobs use OPENAI_API_KEY=fake-for-tests; actions are pinned to full commit SHAs.
code.dependencies: Manifests: pyproject.toml plus a hash-pinned uv.lock (204 package entries, 2646 sha256 hashes; resolved with a 7-day exclude-newer span, uv.lock:1-16; pyproject.toml:274-283). Direct runtime dependencies: 12 (pyproject.toml:9-23) - openai>=3.0.0,<4; pydantic>=2.12.2,<3; griffelib>=2,<3; typing-extensions; requests; websockets>=15,<17; mcp>=1.19,<3; plus 5 'security floors' on transitive packages (httpx2, pyjwt, python-multipart, starlette, urllib3). 20 optional extras (pyproject.toml:42-93): voice, viz, litellm, any-llm, realtime, sqlalchemy, encrypt, redis, dapr, mongodb, docker, blaxel, daytona, cloudflare, e2b, modal, runloop, vercel, s3, temporal (1-6 direct deps each; e2b, modal and temporalio are exact-pinned: pyproject.toml:71-72,78,89; any-llm needs Python >=3.11: pyproject.toml:47-50). Dev group: 35 entries (pyproject.toml:95-132). Example requirement files for examples/realtime/twilio and twilio_sip sit outside the root lock (.github/dependabot.yml:26-38). Dependabot: uv weekly, pip examples, github-actions monthly, all with a 7-day cooldown (.github/dependabot.yml:13-56).
code.security_policy: SECURITY.md exists: private reporting through OpenAI's Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Policy and security.txt PGP info, scope and trust-boundary statements including that tool implementations and local subprocesses use the host application's privileges (SECURITY.md:5,19,25). Contributor security checklist at CONTRIBUTING.md:55-80; CodeQL workflow (.github/workflows/codeql.yml:1-46); CODEOWNERS covers all files (.github/CODEOWNERS:3).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:3 - provider-agnostic: OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs plus '100+ other LLMs'
claim_checks.evidence: Responses and Chat Completions model classes exist (src/agents/models/openai_responses.py, openai_chatcompletions.py). Other providers work only via OpenAI-compatible endpoints or the LiteLLM/Any-LLM adapters, which the docs label 'best-effort, beta' (docs/models/index.md:683-705). The default MultiProvider routes only no-prefix/`openai/`, `litellm/` and `any-llm/` and raises UserError for any other prefix such as `anthropic/` (src/agents/models/multi_provider.py:63-67,214-225). There is no Anthropic-native client in src; Claude appears only via LiteLLM/OpenRouter in an example (examples/model_providers/litellm_provider.py:14-18) and in opt-in integration tests (integration_tests/conftest.py:47-72; integration_tests/README.md:21). The '100+' count is not verifiable from this repo.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:13 - sandbox agents work 'with a container' (docs/index.md:21: 'real isolated workspaces')
claim_checks.evidence: Container isolation exists only for DockerSandboxClient (src/agents/sandbox/sandboxes/docker.py:1855-1906) and hosted clients. The README's own example uses UnixLocalSandboxClient, which runs host processes with no OS-level confinement on Linux and only sandbox-exec filesystem restrictions on macOS (src/agents/sandbox/sandboxes/unix_local.py:266-268,745-774; docs/sandbox/clients.md:17-23). Isolation therefore depends on the backend chosen; code and docs agree, the README wording does not.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:77 - UnixLocalSandboxClient is supported on macOS and Linux; Windows needs Docker or a hosted client
claim_checks.evidence: src/agents/sandbox/sandboxes/__init__.py:13-28 exposes Unix-local only when sys.platform != 'win32'; macOS wraps commands in sandbox-exec (unix_local.py:745-774). The README omits the no-confinement caveat that docs/sandbox_agents.md:31-33 and the class docstring (unix_local.py:1519-1525) state, and by default the client passes the full host environment to commands (unix_local.py:1537; docs/sandbox/clients.md:44).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:19 - Human in the loop: built-in mechanisms for involving humans across agent runs
claim_checks.evidence: needs_approval/on_approval, run interruptions and RunState.to_json/to_string/from_json/from_string with schema version 1.18 including a sandbox payload (src/agents/run_state.py:212,1836,1980-1991,2193,2251,2339). Approval is opt-in: shell, apply_patch and custom tools default needs_approval=False (src/agents/tool.py:1476,1531,1571; src/agents/sandbox/capabilities/tools/shell_tool.py:181-183), and the default Shell capability passes no approval setting (src/agents/sandbox/capabilities/shell.py:50-54; customisable via configure_tools, shell.py:43,60-61).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:20 - Sessions: automatic conversation history management
claim_checks.evidence: Session ABC and SQLiteSession (src/agents/memory/sqlite_session.py:31-43) default to an in-memory database (db_path=':memory:'); durable backends are optional extras (src/agents/extensions/memory/: SQLAlchemy, Redis, MongoDB, Dapr, encrypted; pyproject.toml:52-61). Sandbox workspace persistence is separate: default local snapshots go to a state directory (src/agents/sandbox/snapshot_defaults.py:25-54; runtime_session_manager.py:506-515).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:21 - Tracing: built-in tracking of agent runs
claim_checks.evidence: The default provider registers a BatchTraceProcessor whose BackendSpanExporter posts to https://api.openai.com/v1/traces/ingest (src/agents/tracing/setup.py:52-60; src/agents/tracing/processors.py:46,903-922). It is on by default and includes sensitive data by default (docs/tracing.md:7-13; src/agents/run_config.py:53-56,414-420). The README does not mention the OpenAI-hosted export.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:17 - Tools include hosted tools (README research/coding use cases rely on them)
claim_checks.evidence: Hosted tools such as WebSearchTool are 'only supported with OpenAI models, using the Responses API' (src/agents/tool.py:836-839; docs/tools.md:25-35). Chat Completions-based adapters convert only FunctionTool and raise UserError otherwise (src/agents/models/chatcmpl_converter.py:1017-1037; used by litellm_model.py:555 and any_llm_model.py:875). The sandbox Filesystem capability's apply_patch is a Responses `CustomTool` (src/agents/sandbox/capabilities/tools/apply_patch_tool.py:175; src/agents/tool.py:1563-1565) and Capabilities.default() = Filesystem + Shell + Compaction (src/agents/sandbox/capabilities/capabilities.py:9-10). Compaction injects Responses-style `context_management` into extra_args (src/agents/sandbox/capabilities/compaction.py:188-208; src/agents/sandbox/runtime_agent_preparation.py:107-116), which Chat Completions/LiteLLM/Any-LLM calls forward verbatim (src/agents/models/openai_chatcompletions.py:740; src/agents/extensions/models/litellm_model.py:607-609; src/agents/extensions/models/any_llm_model.py:1351-1352). Inferred from code paths; not executed against any non-OpenAI model.

pyproject.toml:6 requires-python >=3.10; CI matrix Python 3.10-3.14 (.github/workflows/tests.yml:119-130). The any-llm extra is limited to Python >=3.11 (pyproject.toml:47-50; integration_tests/README.md:37).

claim_checks.claim: docs/models/index.md:26-28 (not README) - frontier capability is selected with model='gpt-5.6-sol'; the need names 'GPT-6.1 Sol'
claim_checks.evidence: `gpt-5.6-sol` is known to the code (src/agents/models/default_models.py:66; src/agents/sandbox/capabilities/compaction.py:37) and used by the docs' sandbox coding example (docs/sandbox_agents.md:83; examples/sandbox/docs/coding_task.py:25). No `gpt-6*` / 'GPT-6.1' string exists anywhere in the repo, so 'GPT-6.1 Sol' is not_checkable here: unlisted names get generic ModelSettings (default_models.py:79-87,106-120; docs/models/index.md:109-111) and Compaction falls back to a static 240000-token threshold (compaction.py:12,193-199).

claim_checks.claim: docs/tools.md:941 (not README) - Codex tool resolves `codex` from PATH 'then falls back to the bundled vendor binary'
claim_checks.evidence: src/agents/extensions/experimental/codex/exec.py:275-290 resolves CODEX_PATH, then PATH, then <package>/extensions/vendor/<target-triple>/codex/codex, but no `vendor` directory exists under src/agents/extensions in this revision and pyproject.toml has no build step that adds one (pyproject.toml:140-154), so the codex CLI must be installed separately. Code wins over docs.

risks: Model naming/compat: the repo never mentions GPT-6.1 Sol or any gpt-6* name; the top named tier is `gpt-5.6-sol` (src/agents/models/default_models.py:66; docs/models/index.md:26-28). Unlisted names only get generic ModelSettings (default_models.py:79-87,106-120) and a static 240000-token Compaction threshold (src/agents/sandbox/capabilities/compaction.py:12,193-199); GPT-5.6-specific reasoning mode/context/'max' effort work only on the Responses path and are ignored with a warning on Chat Completions (docs/models/index.md:76-97; src/agents/models/openai_chatcompletions.py:102-125). Nothing in the repo tests a GPT-6.x model.

Claude path is indirect and sandbox-defaults may not fit it: Claude is reachable only through best-effort beta LiteLLM/Any-LLM adapters or OpenAI-compatible gateways (docs/models/index.md:683-705; src/agents/models/multi_provider.py:214-225). The default SandboxAgent capabilities include `apply_patch` as a Responses-only CustomTool and a Compaction capability that injects Responses-style `context_management` (src/agents/sandbox/capabilities/tools/apply_patch_tool.py:175; src/agents/sandbox/capabilities/compaction.py:188-208), while the Chat Completions converter accepts only FunctionTool (src/agents/models/chatcmpl_converter.py:1017-1037). Expect to replace Filesystem/Compaction via configure_tools or capabilities=[...] (src/agents/sandbox/capabilities/filesystem.py:29-52); inferred from code, not run.

Isolation depends on the backend: UnixLocal adds no OS confinement on Linux, only filesystem restrictions via sandbox-exec on macOS (no network isolation), and by default inherits the whole host environment including API keys (docs/sandbox/clients.md:17-23,44; src/agents/sandbox/sandboxes/unix_local.py:752-774,1537). The Docker client exposes only image, ports (bound to 127.0.0.1), network_mode='none', labels and mounts - no CPU/memory/pids/read-only options in SDK code (src/agents/sandbox/sandboxes/docker.py:220-250,1876-1906) - and FUSE/SYS_ADMIN mounts add cap_add SYS_ADMIN plus apparmor:unconfined (docker.py:1891-1901). Docker networking is on by default (docs/sandbox/clients.md:91). Hosted adapters are mock-tested only, not live-validated in CI (examples/sandbox/extensions/README.md:165).

Bounded tool access is opt-in, not default: exec_command takes arbitrary cmd/shell/login/tty arguments with no allowlist (src/agents/sandbox/capabilities/tools/shell_tool.py:114-142); needs_approval defaults to False (src/agents/tool.py:1476,1531,1571); max_turns defaults to 10 but None disables it (src/agents/run_config.py:45; docs/running_agents.md:600); function-tool timeout_seconds defaults to None (src/agents/tool.py:514); archive extraction limits default to none (src/agents/run_config.py:247-252); all tool calls in a turn start concurrently unless max_function_tool_concurrency is set (run_config.py:139-144). The SDK's own docs say applications must authorize tool capabilities and isolate untrusted execution (SECURITY.md:25).

Default telemetry/data flow: tracing is enabled by default, exports LLM and tool inputs/outputs to https://api.openai.com/v1/traces/ingest using the OpenAI key, and is unavailable under ZDR (src/agents/tracing/processors.py:46; src/agents/run_config.py:53-56,414-420; docs/tracing.md:7-13). Runs driven by non-OpenAI models need tracing disabled or a separate key to avoid 401s (docs/models/index.md:609-615). The sandbox Memory capability sends run transcripts to a memory-generating model when the session closes (docs/sandbox/memory.md:51-58).

No research harness: deep-research behaviour exists only as examples that are not shipped in the wheel (pyproject.toml:153-154). They depend on the OpenAI-hosted WebSearchTool (Responses API only, src/agents/tool.py:836-839); citation extraction lives in examples/web_search_utils.py:20-79; the financial example's citation check is an LLM verifier prompted to compare URLs against an allowed list, with no deterministic URL check in code (examples/financial_research_agent/agents/verifier_agent.py:9-21; manager.py:256-273) and a planner on `o3-mini` (agents/planner_agent.py:36); examples/research_bot has no source or citation handling. No published benchmark or task-success data for coding or research quality exists in the repo (searched).

Stability and maintenance: 0.x versioning where minor bumps may break non-beta interfaces and patch releases may change beta features (docs/release.md:3-18); sandboxes were introduced as a 'beta' surface in 0.14.0 (docs/release.md:150-154); the Codex tool and hosted multi-agent model are explicitly experimental (docs/tools.md:892; docs/models/index.md:242), and an in-flight hosted multi-agent response cannot be restored in another process (docs/models/index.md:303). Recent minors carried breaking changes (0.17, 0.20, 0.21 openai v3 + httpx2 migration, 0.22: docs/release.md:24-62,86). RunState schema has been bumped 18 times and older SDKs reject newer state (src/agents/run_state.py:205-258), so resume across SDK versions is one-directional. Pull requests are accepted only from collaborators (CONTRIBUTING.md:7).

Docs-vs-code and operational gaps: the Codex tool's documented bundled-binary fallback does not exist (docs/tools.md:941 vs src/agents/extensions/experimental/codex/exec.py:275-290; codex CLI must be installed and inherits os.environ unless codex_options.env is set, exec.py:225-231). The 30-day cleanup helper for default local sandbox snapshots is defined but only referenced by a unit test (src/agents/sandbox/snapshot_defaults.py:57-84; tests/sandbox/test_snapshot_defaults.py:135-151), so snapshots under the user state directory accumulate. Vercel sessions with mounts cannot be resumed (docs/sandbox/clients.md:186). No checksum/signature/attestation step is configured in the release workflow (.github/workflows/publish.yml:126-158).
